The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click Bakeweek_Studio.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on orders, the week plan and backups.
  4. Follow the three steps on This week: add your first ingredient, save one recipe you bake often, then try an order.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore the sample bakery on This week, or Open the sample bakery in Settings & backup. Sunday Crumb, a made-up microbakery with a bread club, a café account and a Saturday market, fills every screen, and nothing in it is saved. Return to my bakery brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

One week, one plan.

This week adds up every order, standing drop and market day into what to buy, what to bake each day, and whether it fits in your hours.

WordWhat it means
Hands-on timeYour minutes per batch: mixing, shaping, finishing. Proofing and baking on their own don’t count.
BatchOne run of a recipe at its yield. Orders are rounded up to whole batches.
Standing orderA regular drop for a bread club, subscriber or café, added to the order book four weeks ahead.
Available hoursThe hours you can bake each day. The plan warns you when a day needs more.

Your library

What every bake costs.

Add ingredients in Pantry with the pack size and price you pay, then save your tested recipes in Recipes. Every recipe shows its cost, your price and what you keep.

Cost / pieceIngredients and packaging for one piece, at your latest pack prices.
PriceWhat you charge for one piece. Your target margin, card fee and the value of an hour are set in Settings & backup.
KeepsThe share of the price left after costs, before your time.

Orders

Every order, one order book.

Try an order first: it shows the extra hours and costs, and you accept it when the plan works. Orders keep their price, pickup day, balance and the customer’s allergies.

Pre-order menu

Post this week’s menu with a closing time. Copy menu text for your page or group chat; each pre-order joins the plan as it comes in.

Standing orders

Bread clubs, subscriptions and wholesale cafés. Set the schedule once; each drop bakes, shops and packs like any order.

Bake day

Shop, bake, pack.

Shopping totals every recipe in the week, takes off what’s on your shelves, and rounds up to the packs you buy, grouped by supplier.

Batch sheets

Each day’s dough prep and bakes, scaled to the orders, with hands-on minutes. Print batch sheets for the kitchen.

Pack & collect

What goes in each bag, the balance to collect at pickup, and packing tickets with allergies. Kitchen packet prints the lot.

Bakeweek Studio | JPS Digital Pages6

Markets & money

What you really earn.

Reports → Profit & expenses shows sales, ingredients, packaging, fees and the expenses you add, with profit per hands-on hour.

Market days

Plan a market day with the stock you’ll bring, then Record what sold. Sell-through and leftovers tell you how much to bring next time.

Invoices, vendors, bank

Invoice cafés and caterers, send purchase orders to your mill, and import your bank’s CSV: deposits pay invoices, withdrawals pay purchase orders.

Read this one

Keeping your bakery safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every recipe, ingredient, order, customer, invoice and setting. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
A recipe shows no costOne of its ingredients has no pack price. Pantry → edit the ingredient and add what you pay.
A day needs more time than you haveThe week plan says how much more. Move a bake day, raise Available hours, or say no to an order.
Labels look wrongLabels come from the recipe’s ingredients. Check them, and your local cottage-food rules, before you print.
A shopping amount looks oddCheck the ingredient’s pack size and unit in Pantry: the list rounds up to whole packs.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Show the welcome tour again → Show tour.
